Chapter 10: Finishing Well — A Life of Faithfulness.
You know, there’s a quiet beauty in living a life with steady faith—a faith that weathers every season, the good and the hard.
Finishing well isn’t about being perfect or having a spotless record. It’s really about holding on, staying true to what matters, and reaching the end with your heart still open to God.
Picture a man in his later years, looking back on his life. Gratitude and regret both stir in his heart. There were wins, there were failures, times when he felt close to God, and times when he drifted. But what stands out? He always came back. He kept seeking forgiveness, starting over, trusting that grace was more than enough. Those who loved him didn’t just remember his accomplishments—they remembered his humility, his kindness, his steady faith.
Most people don’t realize just how much the way you finish shapes your whole story. The end isn’t just the last page—it’s the lens through which everything else is remembered. The way someone finishes—their attitude, their relationships, their faith—it all leaves a mark.
There’s a beautiful example in the story of a married couple growing old together. As their health faded and routines changed, their love only grew stronger. They prayed side by side, found laughter in the everyday, and held each other up through heartbreak and change. Their children and grandchildren watched and learned—this is what it looks like to love faithfully, all the way to the end.
It’s easy to slip into thinking that our best days are behind us, especially as we age. Maybe you’ve felt that way yourself. But someone after God’s heart knows that every season brings its own purpose. There’s always room to serve, to encourage, to keep growing.
Finishing well means staying involved—never stopping your pursuit of learning, giving, or seeking God. It’s about letting go of mistakes, embracing forgiveness, and looking ahead with hope. I think of a man, facing a terminal illness, who wrote heartfelt letters to his family—sharing love, faith, and his hopes for their future. Those words became a precious legacy, a source of comfort and inspiration.
So, if you’re approaching the end of a chapter, consider this your invitation: finish well. Stay faithful. Keep loving, keep serving, keep trusting. The journey isn’t over until the very last breath—and every single day, you have a new chance to reflect God’s heart to the world.
